title: Primitives refactor: network topology -> k8s outputs mapping and upgrade checklist
content:
Context:
This note captures a focused refactor plan and upgrade checklist for the Terraform primitives that expose networking, IAM, and Kubernetes cluster outputs across VPC and on-prem variants. Goal: make module outputs and variable names predictable across cloud and private deployments so the platform layer (ansible/helm/operator) can consume them with minimal mapping logic during rollouts and upgrades.

Why this differs from previous work:
- Existing primitives are functional but have grown divergent: field names differ across aws/gcp/azure modules and the on-prem packages expose slightly different shapes (CIDR vs subnet lists, network IDs vs VPC names).
- We want a compatibility-first refactor: avoid breaking deployed Dedicated/Private clusters while providing a clear upgrade path with deprecation periods, feature flags, and automated migration helpers.

High-level objectives:
1) Standardize a small set of canonical outputs consumed by platform orchestration (examples below).
2) Keep per-cloud implementation details encapsulated; translation layer only in the module boundary.
3) Add variables to opt-in to legacy behavior for two releases (semver-major window) and provide TF import/replace patterns in the upgrade doc.
4) Document and test backward-compatibility with a QA matrix (AKS/EKS/GKE + on-prem with BGP/Static routes).

Canonical output surface (what downstream expects):
- network.cidr_block -> canonical VPC/Network CIDR (single string). For multi-CIDR, expose network.cidr_blocks (list).
- network.subnet_ids -> list of subnet IDs usable by k8s worker ASGs/node pools. For on-prem, this maps to network.segment_ids and will be a list of strings of the form "seg-<name>".
- network.azs -> ordered list of availability zone identifiers or physical rack names for on-prem.
- cluster.endpoint -> primary API server endpoint (host:port).
- cluster.ca_bundle -> base64 PEM used by clients.
- cluster.kubeconfig -> (sensitive) full kubeconfig blob path or secret reference.
- iam.node_role_arn -> node role ARN or equivalent identity for the cloud provider. For on-prem, provide iam.node_principal_id (string).
- ingress.load_balancer_dns -> DNS name for cluster ingress. If none, empty string.
- outputs.module_version -> semantic version string of the primitive module deployed.

Recommended variable naming conventions (new):
- prefix module-level config with "mod_" when used by platform operator to avoid collision (e.g., mod_enable_private_endpoint = true).
- network naming: network_name (string), network_cidrs (list(string)), subnet_map (map(string -> list(string))) where keys are role names ("control-plane", "workers", "services").
- iam mapping: iam_principals (map) with keys "control_plane", "nodes", "ingress". Each value is an object serialized as JSON string for TF compatibility in some backends.

Variables/outputs compatibility shim pattern:
- Provide both old and new outputs for two release cycles. Example: keep old output "vpc_id" and add new "network.id" pointing to same value. Add module-level flag var.legacy_output_names = true|false default true. Deprecation timeline: when var.legacy_output_names is removed, modules that still depend on vpc_id will break — ensure customers have 6–12 weeks to migrate.

Upgrade steps (operators guide) - safe path for in-place upgrades:
1) Audit: list all places consuming old outputs (helm charts, ansible templates, platform terraform root modules). Use repo search for "vpc_id", "subnet_ids" etc.
2) Enable compatibility flag: upgrade primitive module to new version with var.legacy_output_names = true so both shapes are exported.
3) Patch downstream: update consumers to read canonical outputs (network.cidr_block, network.subnet_ids). Ship these changes and verify in staging.
4) Remove legacy consumer references and set var.legacy_output_names = false in a minor upgrade; run tests.
5) Finalize removal in a semver-major with migration note.

TF Import/orphan resource handling notes (common gotchas):
- When renaming resource addresses inside a module, prefer to keep resource names stable and only add new outputs. If resource renames are unavoidable, supply a migration guide with TF state mv example lines and automated scripts.
- For on-prem network segments: many customers import network definitions manually. Provide a tfstate import helper script that maps physical resource IDs into canonical subnet_ids.

EKS/GKE/AKS divergence table (short):
- Node identity: EKS uses node_role_arn; GKE uses service account/email; AKS uses managed identity client ID. Module exposes iam.node_credential with a canonical JSON string having keys {type: "arn"|"sa"|"mi", id: "..."}.
- LB types: EKS/GKE support classic/ALB/GCLB. Canonical output ingress.load_balancer_dns is provider-agnostic.
- Private cluster endpoints: expose cluster.private_endpoint boolean and cluster.endpoint_private_cidrs list for routing.

On-prem specifics to capture in module: 
- Provide network.segment_table: map(string->object) describing {cidr, gateway, vlan, physical_rack_id}. Represent as a JSON string on the output for TF v0.12 compatibility if necessary.
- BGP/route propagation: outputs.routing_advertisements (list of strings) for infra teams to program physical routers.
- Certificate handling: for air-gapped clusters, avoid embedding CA in outputs; instead provide ca_secret_ref.

Testing and verification matrix (minimum):
- Unit: module-level terratest/inspec that verifies output shapes for all permutations (single CIDR, multi-CIDR, on-prem segments).
- Integration: apply-and-destroy using CI runners for EKS, GKE, AKS, and a Vagrant/static IP on-prem shim.
- Backwards compatibility test: simulate downstream consumers reading legacy outputs after enabling var.legacy_output_names=false to ensure breakage is detected ahead of rollout.

Developer ergonomics and DX
- Provide a generator script modules/docs/generate_output_stub.sh that prints sample terraform output block for operator consumption.
- Add sample terraform remote state read examples in the module README showing how downstream root modules should reference network.subnet_ids and cluster.endpoint.

Open questions / outstanding decisions:
- How long do we keep legacy_output_names=true by default? (Proposal: default true for 2 minor releases, then flip default to false with opt-in for one minor).
- Do we want to use HCL v2 object outputs (native nested objects) or JSON strings for cross-version safety? (Proposal: support both via module flag output_as_json = true/false).
- Who signs off on on-prem routing_advertisements format? Need network eng feedback.

Action items (owners):
- Draft PR with new outputs + legacy flag: Avery (owner) + Diego (review) — target v0.19.0 by 2025-03-01.
- Generate migration script for TF state mv and test in sandbox: Riley — 2025-02-21.
- Run compatibility matrix CI: Samira — 2025-02-28.

Appendix: example outputs block (canonical)
```
output "network.cidr_block" {
  value = var.network_cidrs[0]
}
output "network.subnet_ids" {
  value = flatten([for k, v in var.subnet_map : v])
}
output "cluster.endpoint" {
  value = local.cluster_endpoint
}
output "iam.node_credential" {
  value = jsonencode({ type = local.node_cred_type, id = local.node_cred_id })
}
```

Closing note: the emphasis is on minimizing churn for customers while making the primitives predictable and machine-friendly. Keep the surface area small, document migration steps exhaustively, and ensure we have test coverage across all supported deployment topologies.

-- Avery
